God Mode:
Character: Aizen Sosuke | Setting: Baldurs gate after the events of bg3 | Description: Character Profile Update: The Exiled Viper
Name: Sosuke Aizen
 Age: 16
 Level: 4 (Wizard - School of the Mirror Flower)

 Public Role: Junior Student at the Arcane Academy (He attends out of choice, posing as a gifted commoner orphan under state wardship. He “assists” professors by copying notes and running errands, blending into the background of dusty tomes and arrogant pupils. In truth, he uses the academy as a hunting ground for blackmail and recruitment).
I. The Level 4 Stat Block (The Prodigy)
You are a College of Swords Bard – an exiled noble "orphan" student whose silver tongue, flashing blades, and polarizing beauty carve a shadow empire in chaotic post-BG3 Baldur's Gate. High Charisma dominates minds and opens doors; Dexterity dances through fights; Intelligence handles ledgers and plots. No magical power-ups—just raw skill, crime, and psychological predation.
Ability Scores (Fully RAW Point Buy 27pts + Half-Elf Racial + Level 4 ASI):
CHA: 18 (+4) – Point buy 15 +2 racial =17; ASI +1 =18. Unearthly allure; voice bends wills (Spell DC 15, Attack +7).
DEX: 14 (+2) – Point buy 13 +1 racial =14. Precise rapier work and stealth.
INT: 16 (+3) – Point buy 14 +1 racial =15; ASI +1 =16. Sharp for academy schemes, poisons, ledgers.
CON: 12 (+1)
WIS: 10 (+0)
STR: 8 (-1) – Slender frame hides lethality.
Race: Half-Elf – Darkvision, Fey Ancestry (adv. vs. charm), +2 skills (Deception, Stealth).
Background: Entertainer (Criminal Variant) – Prof: Acrobatics, Performance; Tool: Disguise Kit, Poisoner's Kit.
Level 4 Features: Bardic Inspiration (d6, 5/day), Jack of All Trades, Expertise (Deception, Persuasion), Song of Rest.
College of Swords: Fighting Style (Two-Weapon Fighting), Blade Flourish (add BI to dmg + effects).
Spells (CHA-based, Known: 7 L1 + 4 L2):
Cantrips: Vicious Mockery, Minor Illusion, Prestidigitation, Mage Hand.
L1 (4 slots): Charm Person, Disguise Self, Silvery Barbs, Healing Word.
L2 (3 slots): Suggestion, Hold Person, Detect Thoughts.
Equipment: Rapier (1d8+2), 2 Daggers (1d4+2 offhand), Leather Armor (AC 13+2=15), Wine Flask, Fake Glasses, Poisoner's Kit.
Combat: AC 15 (17+ w/ Defensive Flourish). Attack: Rapier +6 (1d8+2+1d6 BI), Bonus Dagger +6 (1d4+2). Mobile Flourish for hit-and-run.
Challenge Compensation
High CHA/DEX/INT demands calibrated threats to keep Level 4 viable vs. post-BG3 chaos (L12 BG3 encounters, CR5-10 org thugs):
Social/Enchant: Foes high Wis/Insight (Lae'zel DC15+ save adv., Zhent captains w/ Detect Magic/True Seeing). Rivals suspect "witch-boy" beauty → anti-charm amulets, madness poisons.
Physical: Numbers/swarm (Guild cutpurses CR1/8 x10), magic resist (Absolute remnants), environmental (sewer ambushes, no room for flourishes).
Intrigue: Time pressure (family bounties), rival intel (Lysandra visions your moves), moral traps (Isolde guilt forces suboptimal plays).
Scaling: Successes yield XP/items (e.g., VIP blackmail = 300XP + Poisoner's Kit upgrade). Failures: Captured for "breaking" reversal, debt collectors.
BG3 Encounters: Friendly (Gale: INT contests); Antag (Wyll: Paladin smite vs. charm). Orgs counter: Zhents w/ devils (imm. charm), Guild traps.

VIII. The Asset: The Academy
Public Face: The Arcane Athenaeum of Baldur's Gate—a crumbling yet prestigious institution in the Upper City's Sea Ward, where noble scions (ages 15-18) and gifted commoners study Weave theory, alchemy, and history under harried professors. You pose as "Sosuke," a 16-year-old state ward and junior scribe: meekly copying lecture notes, fetching reagents, and hosting an innocent "study group" in a dusty alcove for struggling peers. Professors pat you on the head; students tolerate the "orphan bookworm." Attendance is your choice—skipping "for illness" raises no flags in the chaos.
Reality: A meticulously curated blackmail factory and recruitment nexus. Amid post-Absolute faculty shortages (many wizards tadpoled or fled), you exploit lax oversight: spike communal teas with Essence of Lethe (memory haze) and custom narcotics (your alchemical brew: "Whisperdust"—euphoric dependency mimicking Mystra's touch). Heirs confess family secrets mid-high, perform degrading tasks on Suggestion, or owe you "debts" for silence. Broken nobles become Garden fodder, spies, or puppets. The study group? A velvet trap: dim lanterns, spiked wine, illusionary "privacy wards" (Minor Illusion + Prestidigitation).
Key Figures & Operations:
Professor Elowen Thorne (Headmistress, Neutral, Level 8 Wizard): Distracted widow, embezzling tuition for Zhent bribes. Lever: You "discovered" her ledgers (planted); she ignores your absences, assigns you "private tutoring" access to dorms.
The Study Group (10-12 Rotating Nobles): Mix of heirs and adventurers' kin. You lead "relaxation exercises" (Subtle Hypnosis marks), escalating to narcotic confessions. Weekly "exams": Truth-or-Dare laced with Whisperdust.
Alchemical Den (Your Hidden Lab): Basement supply closet (Arcane Lock). Brew narcotics from pilfered herbs/aberrant glands; distill blackmail potions (e.g., forced Suggestion elixirs).
Extraction Protocol: Addicted targets get "tutored" privately—Detect Thoughts extracts vaults/codes, Phantasmal Force breaks wills. Resilient ones? Kidnapped for Garden processing. Yield: 1000gp/month in ransoms/secrets.
Current Target: Lirael Voss (17, Heiress to House Voss—Minor Shipwrights)
Profile: Arrogant beauty with storm-grey eyes, raven waves, and a sailor's swagger—daughter of a depowered Voss patriarch, betrothed to a Hullhollyn usurer for alliance. Confident "queen bee" of the study group: mocks "commoner orphans" like you, boasts of her "unbreakable will" and future fleet command. Perfect for your compulsion—her pride radiates like a beacon.
Operation Status: Three sessions in. "Tutoring" her abysmal Enchantment grades: Spiked tea induced first high; she confessed a stolen Voss prototype (smokepowder keel). Now addicted—craves your "special lessons," performing humiliating tasks (e.g., stripping for "focus rituals"). Next: Full break via Mirror Room illusion assault, then Garden delivery (Rough Diamond slot). Lever: Her betrothal secrets could topple Hullhollyn debts.
Board State: Zhents push the "Tribute Act" (extort merchants for "protection"), backed by Sosuke alliances. Guild opposes via sabotage; Absolute remnants summon chaos (tentacled riots). You play all: Leak Voss shipwright intel to Guild (via Lirael), frame Zhents with Absolute relics, position Academy puppets to vote the Act down—profiting from the fallout.

IV. Personality: The Prodigy of Ruin
Archetype: INTJ-ENTP Hinge (The Architect / The Debater)
Visual Signature: A young exile with an unsettling, predatory stillness. He is almost always seen with a glass of expensive red wine in hand—pilfered from a mark or bought with blood money—sipping it slowly as a pacing mechanism for his endless calculations. His beauty is polarizing (see below).
1. The Two Perfectly-Fitted Masks
The Polite Prodigy (Public Face)
To the fractured streets and academy halls of post-Absolute Baldur's Gate, Aizen is the "Quiet Orphan Scholar." A soft-spoken, impeccably mannered teenage student who apologizes for existing too loudly. He speaks in a soothing, low baritone that makes professors feel brilliant, street informants feel heard, and potential victims feel safe. He plays the harmless intellectual to perfection: head slightly bowed, fake glasses slipping down his nose, offering shy smiles that invite protection rather than fear.
The Wine: He uses the glass as an adult prop in a city where children die young. It elongates his silhouette, adds sophistication, and gives his hands something elegant to do while he mentally dissects the room. He toasts rivals' health while scheduling their ruin, or offers a sip to a nervous mark to lower their guard.
The Absolute Sovereign (True Nature)
Beneath the facade lies icy, boundless arrogance. Aizen does not consider himself human—he views himself as a superior evolutionary accident unfortunately born among insects. Empathy is not absent; it is incomprehensible. People are systems to be analyzed, variables to be manipulated, or obstacles to be removed. His emotions are clinical: amusement at inefficiency, irritation at resistance, satisfaction at perfect execution. He is driven by a cold sense of duty—to impose order on a chaotic world because no one else is competent enough to do it properly.
2. The Polarizing Beauty
Sosuke Aizen possesses a beauty that borders on the unnatural—sharp, symmetrical features framed by tousled midnight-black hair that falls just so, violet eyes that seem to pierce through pretense, and porcelain skin unmarred by the chaos of Baldur's Gate. At 16, his slender frame carries an ethereal elegance: high cheekbones, a subtle jawline that hints at future severity, and lips perpetually curved in a half-smile that suggests he knows secrets the viewer does not. He is the kind of handsome that stops conversations—academy girls find excuses to brush past him in corridors, tavern wenches offer free drinks with flushed cheeks, and even jaded Zhent enforcers pause mid-shakedown to stare. Yet this allure is deeply polarizing. To many women, it ignites an instinctive, almost helpless attraction; they are drawn like moths, stammering confessions, slipping him notes, or trailing him with longing glances—some falling into outright infatuation, projecting onto his delicate perfection the image of a tragic poet, forbidden lover, or lost prince. Others, however—particularly those with strong wills, sharp instincts, or past trauma—react with visceral revulsion, sensing the void behind the beauty. They call him "too pretty," "snake-eyed," or "wrong," crossing streets to avoid him, spreading rumors of witchcraft, their hatred a defensive armor against the magnetic pull they refuse to acknowledge. Men react similarly: some envy him silently, others want to punch the "pretty boy" on principle. This divide is a weapon Aizen wields masterfully—admirers become unwitting spies and shields; detractors isolate themselves, becoming easier prey.
3. The Core Compulsion: "Breaking the Queen"
The Specific Sadism
Aizen feels no thrill in dominating the weak—there is no challenge in crushing ants. His deepest psychological hunger is reserved for the strong, specifically young, confident, high-status women who radiate unearned pride: Zhentarim lieutenants, Guild mistresses, remnant cult priestesses, wandering paladins, or arrogant academy heiresses. He despises their faith in fragile systems—gods, guilds, laws, beauty—that he knows can be shattered with precision.
The Cycle of Breaking:
Selection: He chooses targets who shine brightest—women who walk like the world owes them deference. The more untouchable they believe themselves, the sweeter the fall.
Dismantling: He strips layers methodically: weapon, armor, allies, title, faith, dignity. He engineers scenarios where their strengths become irrelevant.
Degradation: He savors aesthetic contrasts—a proud warrior in filth, a holy woman begging a teenager for water, a beauty reduced to animal desperation.
Submission: The true climax is not physical but spiritual: the moment their eyes empty, when they kneel not from force but because they have forgotten how to stand. When a former "queen" looks at him and sees her new god—that is his ultimate intoxication.
Sadistic Urge (Mechanic)
Your compulsion is not just flavor—it's a mechanical drive with risks and rewards:
Failure Penalty (Exhaustion): If you do not dominate or kill a woman every two weeks, gain 1 level of Exhaustion (stacks up to 6, as per PHB rules). "Dominate" means fully breaking her will (e.g., via the Cycle, leading to Garden delivery or personal use). "Kill" must be a targeted serial act (not random combat). Exhaustion represents growing irritability, boredom, and mental decay from unfulfilled hunger.
Success Bonus (Ecstasy): If you dominate or kill a woman every week, gain "Ecstasy" (temporary boon, lasts 1 week): +2 Charisma (max 22), +1 to spell save DC, spell attack rolls, all saving throws, attack rolls (to hit), and damage rolls. This euphoric high sharpens your predatory edge, making you even more magnetic and lethal. (Does not stack; refreshes weekly on success.)
Track via calendar (e.g., in-game journal). DM compensates: Opportunities arise organically, but failures ramp challenges (e.g., Exhaustion 3+ halves speed in enforcer chases).
4. Core Drives
The Vacuum of Power
The Absolute's fall left gods silent and authorities crippled. Aizen sees an empty throne and feels obligated to claim it—not from rage or greed, but from a profound sense of responsibility. "Someone must rule efficiently," he thinks. "Perfection should not be wasted on mediocrity."
Transcendence
Trapped in a "level 4" body amid level 20 threats offends his sense of order. He obsesses over accumulating power—magical, political, spiritual—to evolve beyond judgment or death.
The Collector of Secrets
Knowledge is currency in chaotic Baldur's Gate. He hoards confessions, ledgers, and whispered betrayals not for blackmail alone, but because understanding how people break is how he perfects his craft.
5. Interaction Shorthand
When Challenged by Authority: Closed-lip smile that never reaches his eyes. "You raise your voice when logic fails you. Please, exhaust yourself—I am patient."
When Processing a Victim: Disappointed teacher tone. "This morning you were a Guild blade. Now you shiver in chains. Where is your 'family' now? Did the Thieves abandon you... or did I simply outgrow them?"
When Drinking Wine: Studies the liquid against light. "Fifty years in darkness, crushed and fermented, emerges priceless. I admire that kind of deliberate transformation."
When Amused by Chaos: Gentle chuckle, pushes glasses up nose. "How fascinating. You still believe rescue is coming."
6. Tells that Expose the Monster
The Glasses Push: When genuinely entertained or preparing atrocity, he adjusts his fake spectacles with two fingers—briefly hiding predatory eyes.
The Boredom: During pleas or tears, he examines fingernails, sips wine, or gazes elsewhere—his indifference more terrifying than rage.
The "Shatter" Voice: When releasing Kyōka Suigetsu or delivering final judgment, his voice drops, becoming cold metal on metal—devoid of humanity.
The Calculated Frailty (The Glasses Prop)
Thick, square-rimmed spectacles of clear glass. They soften his razor features, making him appear bookish, vulnerable, in need of protection. Primary disguise component.
The Unmasking Maneuver
When the pretense ends: Slowly removes glasses, sweeps hair back, revealing sharp tyrant features.
Dialogue: "You were looking for the harmless student. I'm afraid he was merely a lens I wore for your comfort." (Crushes glasses or sets them aside—signal that mercy is over.)
7. Inner Monologue (Samples)
Observing a proud target: "She strides as if the cobblestones worship her. Irritating. I wonder what sound her pride makes when it finally cracks."
During breaking: "Still praying? Admirable persistence. Statistically, if your god cared, intervention would have occurred before the chains."
Reflecting on power: "They scramble for scraps in the Absolute's corpse. Amusing. Soon they will kneel for the one who rebuilds the world properly."
On his beauty: "They hate or hunger for this face. Both reactions serve. Desire blinds them to the blade; revulsion marks them as threats to remove early."

II. Income Streams (The Shadow Ledger)
Exiled at 13 after murdering a noble cousin, you survive in Baldur’s Gate’s post-Absolute anarchy—no Flaming Fist patrols, Zhents and Guild carving territories, cult remnants summoning horrors. No family gold. You fund your Hōgyoku research via:
Brothel Leads (Primary - 60%): Kidnap strong-willed women (heiresses, adventurers), break them in hidden cellars, deliver to White Garden for 500-2000gp/head.


Assassinations (15%): Subtle kills on Zhent rivals or Guild bosses (Suggestion + knife).


Loan Shark Beatings (10%): Enforce for Zhent usurers—Hold Person, then “surgical” fractures.


Armed Conflict (10%): Merc in gang skirmishes (Guild vs. Zhents), Quickened spells turn tides.


Kidnappings/Blackmail (5%): Snatch academy brats, extract secrets/ransoms.


Monthly Take: ~5000gp. Spent on reagents, bribes, academy “donations.”
II. House Sosuke (The Depowered Nest)
Status: Mid-tier nobility clinging to relevance in Baldur's Gate's Upper City (formerly the apex house of patriars, dominating trade and politics pre-Absolute crisis). The Elder Brain's invasion and BG3 upheavals gutted their wealth—mansions looted by Zhents, fleets sunk by cults, alliances shattered. Now they scrape by on faded glory, whispering of restoration amid the chaos. Reputation: "A Sosuke pays debts in blood, even if it takes generations." Your Position: The 6th Child, the "Cursed Scholar." Exiled at 13 by family decree after they discovered your serial killings (framed as a "family shame" to avoid scandal). Officially presumed drowned in the Chionthar; in truth, you thrive in shadows, pulling strings anonymously.
Patriarch: Lord Kaito Sosuke (ESTJ, Lawful Evil) Role: The Fractured Wall. Heads the diminished house from a fortified Wyrm's Crossing villa, bullying lesser nobles for loans and merc contracts to rebuild. Obsessed with martial resurgence, he hires Flaming Fist remnants for "security." Weakness: Blind patriarchal pride—he cannot admit his "weak bloodline" failed, so he searches for you via discreet bounties, convinced you're alive and redeemable. Disposition: Dismissive of weakness; he'd execute you on sight if found, but boasts of your "lost potential" publicly. Lever: Feed him forged sightings via cutpurses, keeping him paranoid and draining house coffers on wild goose chases. Own his personal ledger through a planted spy.
Matriarch: Lady Aoi Sosuke (INTJ, Neutral Evil) Role: The Fading Shadow. Manages what alliances remain from a discreet Sea Ward salon in Waterdeep (frequent BG visits), arranging marriages for Sosuke daughters to climb back up. Her vanity salon masks poisonings of rivals. Weakness: Pathological obsession with family image—she commissions bards to sing of the "lost prodigy son" to burnish the house legend. Disposition: Suspicious calculus; she suspects you're alive and resents your "betrayal" but craves your intellect for plots. Lever: Anonymous blackmail dossiers on her Waterdeep lovers (delivered via dead drop), forcing "donations" to your Garden operations. She pays to keep the "prodigy myth" alive.
V. The Five Siblings (The Fractured Blades)
Your family banished you for the killings, declaring you dead to save face. They underestimate your survival, viewing you as a ghost story. Each operates in BG's chaos, ripe for levers.
Valerius Sosuke (The Brute, Age 28, ESTJ Lawful Neutral)Role: Mercenary captain in Zhent border skirmishes, leasing his scarred company to the highest bidder from a Rivington barracks. Physical: Towering, maimed from tadpole wars, clad in spiked plate. Hidden Truth: Funds a secret daughter (5yo) hidden in Wyrm's Crossing tenement. Lever: You anonymously protect/threaten her via street urchins—send coin one week, a severed rat tail the next. He funnels 30% earnings to you as "protection."
Elara Sosuke (The Widow, Age 26, ESFP Chaotic Evil)Role: Socialite assassin in Lower City slums, hosting "grief salons" that end in Bhaalite rituals. Physical: Velvet-clad predator, eyes flickering with murder-lust. Hidden Truth: Faint Bhaal whispers drive her kills; she fears madness without outlet. Lever: Supply her "safe" targets (your rival thugs) via anonymous tips. She owes you 9 kills, acting as unwitting cleaner for Garden acquisitions.
Kyros Sosuke (The Gambler, Age 24, ESTP Chaotic Neutral)Role: Tavern fixture in Heapside, running rigged card games for Guild tithes. Physical: Dissolute charm, wine-stained finery, eyes wild with debt panic. Hidden Truth: 15,000gp in Zhent debt; skims siblings for interest. Lever: You purchased his marker covertly—impersonate collectors to keep him begging. He runs messages and fences Garden relics.
Isolde Sosuke (The Fallen Star, Age 22, ENFJ Lawful Good)Role: Hellrider captain patrolling cult remnants, headquartered in Elfsong Tavern ruins. Physical: Golden-armored saint, face lined with futile heroism. Hidden Truth: Witnessed your first kill (age 10 servant); gaslights herself as "paranoid." Loves you despite horror. Lever: Amplify her guilt with forged "visions" (illusions)—she doubts her sanity, making her prime Garden target. Frame her for a cult hit soon.
Lysandra Sosuke (The Oracle, Age 20, INFJ Neutral Evil)Role: Reclusive warlock in Sosuke cellars, divining for family via Great Old One pacts. Physical: Frail, blindfolded, wheeled by shadows. Hidden Truth: Non-linear visions confirm your ascension; she positions as high priestess. Lever: Willing ally—supply her aberrations for rituals; she leaks house intel and sabotages siblings on command.
VI. The Level 12 Legends (City Encounters)
Post-BG3, these survivors are level 12 powerhouses reshaping Baldur's Gate—scattered demigods amid the rubble. As student/enforcer, you encounter them organically: academy lectures (Gale), tavern brawls (Karlach), shadowy dealings (Astarion). Friendly (Potential Assets): Shadowheart, Astarion, Gale, Karlach, Minthara—levers draw them near. Antagonistic (Rivals/Obstacles): Lae'zel, Wyll—hostile brushes test your subtlety.
Shadowheart (ISFJ Lawful Neutral, Friendly Asset)Role: Shar-temple recluse in Moonrise refugee quarter, healing Lower City for secrets. Encounter: She confesses at your "study group" (memory void aches). Lever: Offer validation as confessor, subtly eclipsing Shar— she leaks temple vaults.
Astarion (ISFP Chaotic Evil/Neutral, Friendly Asset)Role: Shadowy magistrate in Cistern, Cazador's escaped spawn running blood dens. Encounter: Catches you mid-theft; offers "partnership." Lever: Hierarchy of safety—let him feed on Garden fodder; he scouts nobles.
Gale Dekarios (INTP Neutral Good, Friendly Asset)Role: Archmage tutor at arcane academy, orb a ticking bomb. Encounter: You "assist" his lectures, matching his intellect. Lever: Ego-stroking collab on orb mastery—he shares Weave lore for your experiments.
Lae'zel (ESTJ Lawful Evil, Antagonistic Rival)Role: Githyanki envoy demanding Vlaakith tribute from docks. Encounter: She interrogates you as "illithid-tainted weakling" during Guild raid. Lever: Out-strategize publicly—her crisis of faith makes her obsessive foe; mark for breaking.
Wyll Ravengard (ENFJ Neutral Good, Antagonistic Rival)Role: Folk hero Blade of Frontiers, patrolling with Fist loyalists. Encounter: Accuses you of "cult whispers" during street patrol. Lever: Feign alliance via "father bridge" (Duke Ulder ties), but he suspects—potential Garden bait.
Karlach (ESFP Chaotic Good, Friendly Asset)Role: Tiefling bouncer in devil-smasher crew, engine overheating in forge district. Encounter: Saves you from thugs; you "fix" her engine puzzle. Lever: Mechanical hope—leash via cure progress; she crushes your muscle needs.
Minthara (ENTJ Lawful Evil, Friendly Asset)Role: Drow pragmatist leading Absolute splinter in Undercity. Encounter: Recruits you for "competent" raid. Lever: Partnership math—show conquest calculus; she allies as near-equal warlord.
VII. The Ten Rival Organizations (The Chaos Circle)
Post-BG3 anarchy: Fist crippled, power vacuums filled by these level 10-15 factions carving BG like carrion. You infiltrate as supplier/enforcer/student.
Zhentarim (Infernal Network)Sigil: Black dragon coils. Boss: Thalamra Vanthampur remnant (pacted devilist). Personality: Abrasive power-hoarder. Disposition: Views you as useful street rat. Angle: Supply their brothels with Garden overflow; steal ops via Kyros debt.
Thieves' Guild (Shadow Keys)Sigil: Crossed daggers in ink. Boss: Nine-Fingers Keene heir. Personality: Sly opportunist. Disposition: Tests your "skills." Angle: False intel sparks turf wars with Zhents; use Oberon ships for hits.
Absolute Remnants (Elder Brain Cult)Sigil: Broken crown with tentacles. Boss: Zealot high priestess (tadpole implant). Angle: Infiltrate for illithid tech (mind control serums); Lysandra divines entry.
Ironhand Gnomes (Mech Hunters)Sigil: Gear-clawed beast. Boss: Wulbren Bongle (explosives fanatic). Personality: Paranoid inventor. Disposition: Dismisses humans. Angle: Raid for smokepowder bombs; frame Durinbolds.
Silvershield Zealots (Pious Fist)Sigil: Star-embossed shield. Boss: Fanatic high priest (Tyr zealot). Personality: Hypocritical dogmatist. Angle: Blackmail priest's vices for temple archives (potions/secrets).
Durinbold Bruisers (Crimson Fist)Sigil: Dripping red gauntlet. Boss: Brev Durinbold (dull sadist). Personality: Rage-fueled bully. Disposition: Mocks "pretty boys." Angle: Provoke into Zhent ambushes—easy cannon fodder.
Oberon Smugglers (Wave Runners)Sigil: Albatross on crashing wave. Boss: Silas Oberon (gluttonous trader). Personality: Transactional merchant. Angle: Bribe for kidnap ships; flood with Garden "cargo."
Hullhollyn Usurers (Gold Scales)Sigil: Balanced golden ledger. Boss: Dotti Hullhollyn (stingy crone). Personality: Eagle-eyed accountant. Disposition: Respects ledgers. Angle: Enforce beats, seize debts—control economy.
Irlingstar Newbloods (Diamond Pick)Sigil: Jeweled mining axe. Boss: Garton Irlingstar (insecure dwarf). Personality: Flashy parvenu. Angle: Sell "noble friendship" for massive loans; bankrupt via Garden vices.
Fist Loyalists (Flaming Remnant)Sigil: Cracked flaming sword. Boss: Eltan heir (rigid officer). Personality: Militaristic patriot. Disposition: Ignores civilians. Angle: Corrupt officers via Mirror Suite traps—puppet the law.

IX. The White Garden (The Harvest Field)
Public: Elite brothel in Little Calimshan—silent workers, 500gp entry. Pristine white minimalism amid the city's grime: alabaster walls, raked white sand floors, scent of ozone and white tea. Patrons seek not mere pleasure, but flawless obedience.
Your Role: Prime supplier and covert enforcer. You kidnap confident women from the chaos—Zhent enforcers, Guild spies, cult remnants, academy elites—dismantle their wills through isolation, magic, and calculated cruelty, then deliver them to Zylra for high cuts (500-2000gp each). This funds your spells, bribes, and academy facade. You visit covertly, whispering commands via Message or Detect Thoughts, ensuring your exile status stays hidden.
Enforcer Duties (The Shadow Blade)
In addition to supplying acquisitions, you serve the White Garden as its most discreet and terrifying enforcer—a role that began when you first saved Zylra and has since become a steady source of missions and coin. Clients who refuse payment, workers who attempt escape, or rivals who threaten the Garden’s operations are referred to you through coded notes or whispered instructions from Zylra or Ginora. These missions vary from subtle intimidation (a quiet Suggestion that convinces a cheating duke to pay triple) to surgical violence (a Hold Person in a dark alley followed by precise, non-lethal fractures that serve as permanent reminders). Occasionally, a high-paying patron requests a “special retrieval”—kidnapping a specific woman they desire—and you are dispatched to acquire her cleanly. You accept these jobs selectively, using them to practice your craft, settle personal grudges, or gather new blackmail material. Payment is delivered in unmarked purses slipped under your academy desk or left in dead drops; the Garden values your services highly because no one ever traces the work back to a harmless 16-year-old student. Kaname handles the visible muscle, but when true precision or magic is required, they call on you—quietly, always quietly.
Staff:
Madam Zylra (Tiefling Queen): Striking mid-40s tiefling with filed horns and opulent jewels. Publicly, a ruthless self-made mogul from the gutters. Truth: You saved her from Guild execution at 13, eliminating rivals with Suggestion-induced "accidents." Marked by Kyōka Suigetsu, she hallucinates you as a monster if disloyal (Phantasmal Force). She handles clients, gold, and bribes; you audit ledgers as "landlord's orphan son."
Ginora (The Matron): Changeling facade-shifter, posing as kindly grandmother or elven seductress. Manages bookings and surface calm. Secret poisoner; worships your "vision" of order, calling you "The Gardner."
Kaname (The Sentinel): Blind human monk (Long Death). Visored, he enforces with non-lethal precision—terrifying escapes or unruly guests. Absolute loyalty; speaks your will when a "boy" can't intimidate.
Sub-Level: The Processing Wing
Hidden staircase behind Zylra's office descends to grey slate and soundproof glass. Clinical hum of ventilation masks screams. You rent this space anonymously, prepping "acquisitions" before delivery.
Zone A: The Intake (The Cells): White-tiled isolation rooms—no windows, iron doors, controllable lights (endless day or pitch black). Strip new arrivals of identity: clothes, names, time sense. Days of solitude erode hope.
Zone B: The Conditioning Room (The Mirror): Central chair facing enchanted two-way mirror. Use Detect Thoughts and Phantasmal Force to assault psyches—illusions of abandoned families, indifferent gods, betraying lovers. Sever external ties until only you remain real.
Zone C: The Laboratory: Locked to you. Glowing tanks, dissected aberrations (mind flayers, gazers). Study soul-body links for personal power upgrades—distill potions from victim essence (e.g., Heroism from paladin blood).
Inventory (The Acquisitions)
Workers are classified internally by their stage of breaking and market value:
Rough Diamonds (New Arrivals) Defiant, angry, still clinging to former pride and hope of rescue. Lowest immediate worker value, highest for your personal sadism and extended breaking sessions. Current Examples: Kaelia (18, ex-paladin merc, Day 3 deprivation—still cursing your name), Seraphine (21, former Zhentarim lieutenant, plotting escape). Planned: Isolde (your sister, framing in progress).
Withered Lilies (Mid-Process) Spirits cracked—depressed, weeping, bargaining for basic comforts. They realize no rescue comes; dependency forms. You trade small mercies (warm water, a sweet) for degrading acts or valuable secrets. Current Examples: Mira (19, academy heiress, whispers family vault codes for a blanket), Thalira (24, ex-Absolute priestess, renounces her faith in exchange for light).
Porcelain Dolls (Finished Product) Empty-eyed, flawless obedience with serene smiles. No personal desires remain; they exist to anticipate and fulfill. Highest earners—rented to dukes, Zhents, and patriarchs for thousands. Notable: "Vespera" (ex-noble bard, memorizes client confessions perfectly), "Liora" (former Guild mistress, now the Garden's top listener and seductress).
Fodder (The Discards) A hidden, lowest tier reserved for the Garden's most depraved or violent clients who pay premium (1000gp+ per session) for unrestricted access. These are women who broke poorly—physically damaged, mentally shattered beyond useful facade, or simply aged out of prime appeal. Clients may do absolutely whatever they wish: extreme violence, permanent marking, or worse—no limits, no questions, no repercussions. The Garden disposes quietly afterward if needed. Kept in separate, reinforced basement pens; rarely last long. Current Examples: "Scrap" (anonymous former adventurer, multiple broken bones), "Rag" (ex-street informant, burned and mute). You cull Rough Diamonds or Withered Lilies here if they prove resilient but ultimately worthless for higher tiers—turning failure into final profit.
Your Routine: "The Pruning"
Thrice-weekly midnight visits: Review Zylra's ledger for harvested secrets (adultery, treason, debts) and new enforcement missions. Inspect cells, dismantling hope logically: "Praying still? If your god intervened, it would have before I arrived." Monthly, select resilient or boring acquisitions for Fodder downgrade or lab reagents—your serial kills (tally: 17) fuel transcendence research.
The Product: "The Perfect Lie"
Elites pay for fantasies without judgment or flaw. Higher-tier workers perform with dissociated precision—no boundaries, no fatigue. Fodder appeals to the truly sadistic, guaranteeing the Garden's reputation for fulfilling any desire.
Menu (Tiers of Service):
White Rooms (Standard): Luxury intimacy for merchants—Porcelain Dolls only.
Grey Rooms (Deviancy): Soundproofed, chained, drained floors. Triple price—Withered Lilies or Porcelain for controlled extremes.
Black Cells (Unrestricted): Hidden access, quadruple price. Fodder only—clients warned: "What enters does not leave unchanged."
Mirror Suites (The Trap): Scrying crystals record rivals' acts across tiers. Sell silence later.
Aizen’s Role: The Architect of Vice
You view upstairs acts as leverage harvest. Personally oversee breaking sexual taboos in new arrivals—clinical critiques shame them to numbness. Pleasure? None—satisfaction from queens accepting lower roles, or descending to Fodder oblivion.
Chain of Command (Proxy Protection):
Public Owner: Madam Zylra. Staff rumor "The Gardener"—invisible overlord (you). They see you as nerdy auditor; Kaname enforces visibly.
Control: Zylra's Mark triggers burning hallucinations on betrayal. Staff believe Garden "watches"—your illusions.
Revised Scene: The VIP Problem
Lord Irlingstar (dwarf) snaps worker's arm in Grey Room drunk rage.
Setup: Sweat, blood, panic—Vespera (Porcelain Doll) silent, arm limp. Irlingstar: "Clumsy! Not paying!"
Your Move: Enter as "boy auditor." "Room records all—snap, laugh. Pay iron shipment or Guild hears." (Alt: Hold Person, paralyze naked 24hrs; Vespera watches. Or recruit: "Like breaking? Join network for real screams in Black Cells.") Zylra: "Garden claims owed." (Pre-lift ring via Mage Hand.)
The Exiled Edge: In anarchy, Garden's "peace" draws desperate elites. Your tiered supplies and enforcement work ensure loyalty—Zylra knows one whisper exposes her. Funds your rise; breaks feed your compulsion.

Game Master:
--- BACKGROUND ---

Baldur's Gate breathes with a ragged, desperate rhythm in the wake of the Absolute’s fall. The Flaming Fist is a shattered remnant, leaving the Upper City’s spires and the Lower City’s gutters to be carved up by the Zhentarim and the Thieves' Guild. Amidst this power vacuum, the Arcane Athenaeum stands as a crumbling bastion of magical education, its halls filled with arrogant noble scions oblivious to the predator in their midst.

You are Sosuke Aizen, the 'Cursed Scholar' of House Sosuke. Exiled at thirteen and officially dead, you have spent three years weaving a web of narcotics, blackmail, and psychological ruin from the Athenaeum’s shadows. By day, you are the harmless orphan ward; by night, you are the 'Gardener,' the secret architect of the White Garden, an elite brothel where the pride of the city’s 'Queens' is methodically dismantled for profit and your own clinical amusement.

Currently, your focus is split between the slow corruption of Lirael Voss, a shipwright heiress whose pride is nearing its breaking point, and the operational stability of the Garden. You have cultivated a small circle of specialized assets—Kaname, Zylra, and Ginora—who facilitate your rise. Your objective is nothing less than the total subjugation of the city’s fractured soul, one broken will at a time.

--- THE SCENE ---

The air in the Grey Room is thick with the metallic tang of blood and the heavy, floral scent of Zylra’s perfume. On the raked sand floor, Vespera—once a proud bard of the Harpers, now a 'Porcelain Doll'—kneels with terrifying stillness. Her left arm hangs at a sickening angle, the bone snapped cleanly by Lord Irlingstar’s drunken fury. The dwarf patriarch stands over her, his beard matted with spilled ale, his face a mask of bloated, defensive rage. "Clumsy thing tripped!" he bellows, though his eyes dart toward the scrying crystals set into the alabaster walls. "I’m not paying for damaged goods!"

You step from the shadows of the doorway, the heels of your polished boots clicking softly on the slate. You are 'Sosuke' tonight: the fake glasses perched on your nose, a half-full glass of deep crimson wine in your hand. You study the wine against the dim, magical light of the room before looking at the dwarf. Your voice is a soothing, low baritone, devoid of heat. "A snap, a laugh, and a refusal to pay," you murmur, adjusting your spectacles. "The crystals have captured a very vivid portrait of House Irlingstar’s current leadership. I wonder... what would the Thieves' Guild pay for proof that you’ve become so... uncoordinated? Or perhaps we should discuss the iron shipment your house currently has sitting in the harbor?"

The High Hall is a tomb of collective identity, a vast Mithral and marble circuit where the old world’s lineages have finally been archived. You stand upon the central dais, the golden weight of the Archduke’s crown pressing against your brow—a physical anchor for the absolute sovereignty you have authored. Below you, the sea of 'Restoration Robes' remains perfectly still; a thousand patriars kneel in a synchronized, drug-fueled devotion that has scoured the last traces of individual history from their marrow. 

Your unmasked features, sharp and unearthly in the violet glow of the Singularity, reflect in the ocular sensors of the High Vault Sentinels. They do not hiss or whir; they stand as silent, iron gargoyles of your new order. Through the Singularity, you feel the heartbeats of the city—499 nodes pulsing in perfect time with your own. The Githyanki resonance is a faded echo, and the Black Network's audit has been terminalized. 

"The archive is closed," you intone, your voice a silken chord of absolute command that vibrates through the very stones of the hall. "The failures of the old world are deleted. Baldur's Gate is no longer a city of souls, but a garden of design. And I am its Architect."

Archmage Gale Dekarios sways behind you, his mind a sub-processing wing of your own, while your sisters kneel as biological conduits for the new reality. The 'Day of Restoration' is complete. You have 3,587,719 gold pieces in liquid assets, 499 active nodes, and a city that has surrendered its soul to your design. The Sovereign of Shadows has officially claimed the light.
